maria_dev: quick async: small compat question for the canary — when a client supplies stop sequences + max_tokens + logprobs with streaming=true, do we guarantee that a generated stop sequence will take precedence over hitting max_tokens (i.e., final response finish_reason='stop_sequence')? also: do we include logprobs for the stop token itself? cc @aj @simon_k

aj: short answer: the contract is that the final response semantics match sync behavior — stop should win if generated. streaming frames may not show the stop immediately, but final payload should. regarding logprobs: we try to include logprobs up to the final token (including stop) in the completed response; streaming frames sometimes omit interim logprobs.

simon_k: confirming Aj. we include logprobs for the stop token when the stop is generated. if max_tokens exhausts first, we mark finish_reason='length'. edge case: if the stop text is already present in the prompt (prefix stop), results can be surprising — add a regression for that.

lisa: ran a tiny canary earlier today. stream sent a frame that cut before the stop, but the final meta said stop_sequence and logprobs included the stop token. snippet below.

lisa: ```
Request:
{ "prompt": "hello\\nEND", "max_tokens": 5, "stop": ["END"], "logprobs": 5, "stream": true }
Final response meta:
{ "finish_reason": "stop_sequence", "tokens": ["hello", "\\n", "END"], "logprobs": [ ... ] }
```

aj: nice. two quick followups: 1) how does this interact with temperature/top_p? stop is a generated token — sampling params can make it more or less likely, so document that. 2) do we need to call out behavior if both stop and max_tokens occur on the same token (tie-break)?

maria_dev: good points. for the canary matrix I'll sweep temp={0.0,0.7} x top_p={1.0,0.6} x stop_present={true,false} x max_tokens small. want to catch any nondeterministic ties. i'll add the tests to params-interop. ping me when contract doc is updated.

simon_k: I'll add a short API note: \"stop sequences may be produced or not depending on sampling parameters; when a stop is produced, final response finish_reason=\\"stop_sequence\\" and returned logprobs include tokens up to and including the stop token.\" Also mention tie-break: we currently favor stop when both occur on same token index (we treat generation producing the stop as the trigger).

buildbot: deploybot: canary tests queued: build/params-interop/2387654321

maria_dev: :thumbsup: thanks — if anyone hits a counterexample (esp with temp=0.0 vs 0.7), drop it here and i'll include in the bug matrix. tagging @lisa to add that snippet to the test harness."
